title: Gravel Calculator
metaDescription: Convert a driveway, path, or drain into cubic yards and tons of gravel or stone. Edit the density, then split a base layer from the surface stone.
secondaryKeywords: how many tons of gravel in a yard
how much does a yard of gravel weigh
intent: Convert an area and depth into cubic yards and tons of gravel or crushed stone for a driveway, path, or drain.
registerRow: Keyword register (estimates): gravel calculator — volume 4, competition ease 2, ad value 2, fit 5, priority 16
intro: Estimate cubic yards and tons of gravel for a driveway, path, or drain. Replace the density with your supplier's figure, or add a separate surface layer.
heroAlt: Cross-section of a driveway: a thicker base layer of gravel under a thinner surface layer, held between two edges.
uniqueAddition: Layered driveway mode with its own depth and density for the base and the surface, a density-source field, and a table of common driveway sizes.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.label: Mode
inputs.help: Single layer uses one depth and one density. Layered driveway adds a surface course on the same area.

inputs.name: shape
inputs.label: Shape
inputs.help: Rectangle uses length and width. Circle uses width as the diameter. Enter sq ft uses the Area box.

inputs.name: length
inputs.label: Length
inputs.help: Longest side of a rectangle, from 1 to 500 ft. Left unused for a circle or when you enter square feet.

inputs.name: width
inputs.label: Width
inputs.help: Shorter side of a rectangle, or the diameter of a circle, from 1 to 100 ft. Left unused when you enter square feet.

inputs.name: area
inputs.label: Area
inputs.help: Used only when Shape is Enter sq ft. From 1 to 50,000 sq ft.

inputs.name: depth
inputs.label: Depth
inputs.help: Gravel thickness. On a layered driveway this is the base course. The 4 inch start is a placeholder, from 1 to 24 inches. Ask your supplier or a local guide before you order.

inputs.name: surfaceDepth
inputs.label: Surface depth
inputs.help: Top course, used only for a layered driveway, from 1 to 12 inches. The 2 inch start is a placeholder, not a measured spec.

inputs.name: density
inputs.label: Density
inputs.help: Short tons in one cubic yard. 1.40 is an unverified estimate. Replace it with your supplier's tons-per-yard for this stone. Allowed range is 1.00 to 2.00.

inputs.name: surfaceDensity
inputs.label: Surface density
inputs.help: Tons per cubic yard for the surface stone. Used only in layered mode, from 1.00 to 2.00. It starts at the same 1.40 estimate.

inputs.name: densitySource
inputs.label: Density source
inputs.help: Estimate means 1.40 is a stand-in. Choose Supplier figure after you type the number your yard gave you. This choice does not change the math.

inputs.name: waste
inputs.label: Compaction / waste
inputs.help: Extra material for compaction and an uneven base, from 0 to 30 percent. 10 percent is an assumption, not a measured compaction rate.

sources.title: NIST Handbook 44 (2026), Appendix C: General Tables of Units of Measurement
